text.title: Incident Comms Templates Internal External Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete `IncidentCommsBundle` for a checkout API with a three-row matrix, four drilled templates and a P1 incident run from Investigating to Resolved in 91 minutes, with a note on every non-obvious value, and one bad bundle showing what the validator prints and what the commander sees beyond it.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: checkout-api serves EU, US and APAC customers with a 99.9% SLA for three enterprise accounts. On 2026-05-12 at 09:02 CEST a payment-router configuration push breaks checkout for EU customers. Ihor is incident commander, Dana is comms lead, Olena owns the bundle. The templates were last drilled on 2026-04-20.

example.title: checkout-api bundle 1.3.0 with INC-2041 resolved
example.note: The P1 row lists all four audiences and `audiences_sent` matches it exactly; P3 is internal-only, so a P3 never triggers the 40,000-recipient email. P1 includes `status_page`, which the highest severity must (r-severity-audience-matrix).

First status-page post at minute 8 and the email at minute 12, both inside the 15-minute P1 deadline; status-page gaps are 28, 27 and 28 minutes against a 30-minute interval, and every non-Resolved update ends with "next update by" (r-first-post-deadline-and-cadence).
States run Investigating, Identified, Monitoring, Resolved; each carries a CEST timestamp, the impact in customer terms and a matching component status (r-status-page-lifecycle-states).

No external text names the payment router, the PSP, a host or a cause until Resolved; the Identified post says "the fault is isolated", not what it is. The `review` flags are all false and Dana approved every send (r-no-speculation-external).
The internal post is where "payment-router config push at 08:58" lives, with Ihor as commander, two owned actions and a 09:30 checkpoint (r-internal-post-fields).

The exec brief is 78 words, five fields, revenue and SLA exposure in numbers, one decision only an executive can make, and an honest "unknown, next update at 09:40" for the ETA (r-exec-brief-one-screen).

Resolved states 09:02 to 10:01 CEST, the scope, the rollback, and a report date three days out; the post-incident email went 54 hours after the end, inside the 72-hour P1 deadline (r-resolution-and-postmortem-commitment).

Every token in the four bodies is in `token_list`, and no filled text contains a double-brace token or a comment (r-placeholders-resolved-before-send). `last_drilled` 2026-04-20 is 22 days before the incident (r-quarterly-drill).

example.title: What the validator and the commander reject
example.note: Validator output (schema): `$.templates.customer_email.body: ... does not match pattern '\{\{next_update_at\}\}'`, `$.incidents[0].updates[0].text: matches forbidden 'not' schema` (the unresolved `{{impact}}` token), `$.incidents[0].updates[0].review.unconfirmed_cause: must equal False, got True`, `$.incidents[0].updates[0].review.internal_names: must equal False, got True`, `$.incidents[0].updates[0].approved_by: matches forbidden 'not' schema`, `$.incidents[0].updates[0].component_status_matches_text: must equal True, got False`, `$.incidents[0].updates[0].next_update_at: expected string, got NoneType`, `$.incidents[0].updates[0].text: ... does not match pattern '(?i)next update (by|at) '`, `$.incidents[0].internal_post.commander: matches forbidden 'not' schema`, `$.incidents[0].internal_post.actions_in_flight: 0 items, minItems=1`, `$.incidents[0].exec_brief.eta: 'soon' does not match pattern ...`, `$.incidents[0].exec_brief.word_count: 240 violates maximum=150`, `$.incidents[0].exec_brief.technical_narrative: must equal False, got True`.

With those fixed, the cross-field block reports: `severity_matrix[P1]: the highest severity must include status_page (r-severity-audience-matrix)`, one `token ... is not in token_list (r-placeholders-resolved-before-send)` line per exec-brief and internal-channel token missing from the five-entry list, `incidents[0]: status_page was sent but the P1 row does not list it`, `customer_email is in the P1 row and received nothing`, `exec_brief is in the P1 row and received nothing (r-severity-audience-matrix)`, `first external post at 48 min, deadline for P1 is 15 (r-first-post-deadline-and-cadence)`, `170 min between status-page updates, interval for P1 is 30; post 'no change' instead (r-first-post-deadline-and-cadence)`, `status page says Resolved but no resolved block with start, end, scope, fix and postmortem date (r-resolution-and-postmortem-commitment)`, and `templates.status_page last drilled 190 days before the incident; stale over 90 (r-quarterly-drill)` (likewise for internal_channel).

What the commander sees beyond the validator: a page that told EU customers "affecting {{impact}} customers" 48 minutes in, then named a database host and a cause the postmortem may contradict, then went silent for nearly three hours and closed with a "resolved" that gives no window for anyone's SLA claim; an internal post with "team" in charge and nothing in flight; an exec brief that will produce the reply-all "so is it fixed?"; and a customer email template that, had it been sent, promises to "keep you posted" with no time attached.
